You are working in the Rust crate "musicrs" (MUSIC DOA estimation). Read CLAUDE.md first and follow it (edition 2024, cargo fmt defaults, small logical commits each building and passing tests).

Setup (do this first, in your working directory):
  git switch -c fix/ifb-memory 6e41e8b
Base is commit 6e41e8b (tip of feat/test-gaps-3), NOT main. Do not touch any other branch, do not push, do not open PRs, do not merge.

Build hygiene: the machine is small (3 cores). Prefix EVERY cargo command with
  CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/claude-1000/-home-orchid-projects-musicrs/860b07ee-3f92-4815-ab52-690d0ae10c8e/scratchpad/target-agents
(shared with other agents; cargo's lock may make you wait — that is expected, do not delete the lock or the dir).

Before finishing, all of these must pass on your branch:
  cargo fmt --check
  cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
  cargo test -- --include-ignored
Add regression tests for behaviour changes (unit tests in src/ or the relevant file in tests/, e.g. tests/errors_test.rs for new errors — every public MusicError the API returns is tested there). Keep doc comments, README and CLAUDE.md accurate for what you change (CLAUDE.md lists tests and the MusicError contract).

Commit messages: imperative subject line like the repo's history (see git log), body explaining why, and end each commit message with the line:
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Keep the diff minimal and focused on your task — other agents are changing other parts of src/music.rs and src/stft.rs on parallel branches, so do not refactor or reformat unrelated code.

Final report (short): branch name, commit hashes + subjects, the exact test/clippy/fmt results, and anything you decided or could not do.

YOUR TASK:
Two issues in MusicEstimator::ifb_music_spectrum (src/music.rs):
(a) Memory: it builds the Vec "covs" holding every active bin's n_mics x n_mics cross-spectral matrix at once before the per-bin silence check/loop, so peak memory is about n_mics^2 * nfft/2 * 16 bytes. Compute each bin's covariance lazily inside the per-bin loop so only one is alive at a time. Results must be bit-for-bit identical (golden tests in tests/golden_test.rs and tests/ifb_test.rs/broadband_test.rs pin this). Note the "strongest" power is computed from the STFTs, not from covs, so it can stay before the loop.
(b) Duplicate entries in the caller's `bins` slice are each processed and counted in the geometric mean, silently weighting them. Deduplicate the active bins (sort + dedup; order does not affect the geometric mean) and document it on the `bins` argument. Add a test that Some(&[a, b]) and Some(&[b, a, a, b, b]) give identical spectra on data where both bins carry signal (e.g. a two-tone signal on bins of nfft 160).
Make these two separate commits.

</system-reminder>

input.code:
await $`cd ${W} && git commit -qam "Build IFB cross-spectral matrices one bin at a time

ifb_music_spectrum collected every active bin's n_mics x n_mics
cross-spectral matrix into a Vec before the per-bin loop, so peak
memory grew with n_mics^2 * nfft / 2. Each matrix is used only once,
so compute it inside the loop instead; the arithmetic is unchanged and
the spectra stay bit-for-bit identical.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && git log --oneline -1`.text();
const [bb, syn, ls] = await Promise.all([$`cd ${W} && cat tests/broadband_test.rs`.text(), $`cd ${W} && grep -n "fn \|ifb_music_spectrum" tests/synthetic_test.rs tests/ifb_test.rs tests/common/mod.rs`.text(), $`cd ${W} && grep -n "ifb\|IFB" README.md CLAUDE.md`.nothrow().text()]);
({bb, syn, ls})
